einzeiler: How chronic stress harms your brain and body, and what you can do about it.
kurzfassung: Professor Carmine Pariante explains how the human body reacts to stress and why modern chronic pressure differs from acute ancestral threats. He discusses the biological links between stress, inflammation, and health risks like heart disease and depression. Finally, he shares evidence-based strategies for coping with stress, such as exercise, social connection, and acceptance.
stichpunkte: Stress is defined as a mismatch between the challenges we face and our perceived ability to cope with them.
Acute stress activates the sympathetic nervous system and triggers cortisol release, preparing the body for immediate fight or flight.
Unlike ancestral acute stress, modern psychosocial stress is continuous, leading to chronic elevation of cortisol and inflammation.
Chronic stress increases the risk of serious health conditions, including metabolic disorders, weight gain, diabetes, and heart disease.
High inflammation from chronic stress can shut down the brain's reward system, contributing to fatigue, anxiety, and depression.
Unhealthy coping mechanisms like alcohol and excessive phone scrolling only numb the symptoms temporarily without resolving the root issue.
Evidence-based ways to manage stress include regular physical exercise, spending quality time with friends and family, and cultivating acceptance.

clips.hook: What happens in your body when a predator approaches?
clips.text: The sympathetic nervous system triggers an immediate physical reaction that increases heart rate and directs blood toward the muscles for quick action.

clips.hook: Why continuous pressure keeps your biological stress systems turned on.
clips.text: Persistent daily worries cause baseline blood pressure and cortisol levels to remain elevated for extended periods rather than returning to normal.

clips.hook: The hidden toll of living with unmanaged stress
clips.text: Carrying heavy stress creates physical damage in the body while simultaneously straining relationships with the people closest to you.

clips.hook: Why trying to measure your cortisol levels is a waste of time
clips.text: Popular attempts to track and modify cortisol miss the point, because effective stress management focuses on practical lifestyle changes instead.

clips.hook: Can physical exercise really help you cope with mental stress?
clips.text: Regular physical activity reduces inflammation and provides a powerful mental outlet for managing daily pressure.

beschreibung:
Growing up, many of us were taught to just stay calm and carry on - as if stress was all in the mind, with no real effect on the body. But chronic stress can change your brain, raise your risk of heart disease, and even shorten your life.

In this episode, we ask: what happens when a stress response built to last minutes never switches off?

Today, Professor Carmine Pariante, one of the world's leading researchers on stress, helps us understand what’s happening in your body during a stressful moment and why chronic stress disrupts sleep, appetite, and energy levels. Carmine also explains how worried you should be about cortisol, and whether "cortisol face" and "cortisol belly" are backed by evidence.

By the end, you’ll understand why stress can be so powerful, when it becomes harmful, and have some evidence-based ways to manage it.

Next time you reach for wine, your phone, or something sweet after a hard day, ask yourself: is this helping you cope, or helping you avoid how you feel?
